fields.note: Amr ibn Hurayth narrates praying with the Prophet and hearing the supplied recitation in Fajr, still vividly heard. Keep the actual transliterated Quran quotation as part of this reported recitation and preserve the source missing subject-link wording.

The entire Arabic-script recitation is actually quoted within the Urdu narration and stays. Only the attached footnote marker is apparatus; it must not remove any Quran words or the narrator memory clause.

Abdullah ibn Saib reports actual Fajr recitation of Surah Muminun, the mention of Isa, cough and bowing. The Surah title and reference to the verse content are integral event description, not appended bibliographic locators.
The full Urdu independently gives the named recitation and cough/bowing event. Preserve the title and Isa clause; only the terminal footnote marker is context.

The source-named Abdullah ibn Khubayb uncle reports the gathering, wetness on the Prophet head, happiness question and wealth/health/cheerfulness replies. Keep the uncle unnamed; wetness does not authorize an inferred bath.
The full Urdu gives the same actually read narrative and replies. Preserve the anonymous uncle and questioner, all qualifications, and only separate the terminal source footnote marker.

Qays reports their old samsara name, the Prophet better merchants address and charity instruction alongside oaths/idle talk. Dalal in parentheses is a dictionary gloss, separate from the actual report.
The own Urdu report includes the old source term and the complete Prophetic instruction. Dalal gloss and the terminal footnote marker are context, while all narration words remain.
Rifaa narrates the morning merchant scene, call, their attentive look and neck movement, and resurrection warning with the pious/good/truthful exception. Retain every actual exception and action.
Read the complete scene and warning. Two separate occurrences of the same numeral/footnote glyph appear, one after the neck movement and one at the end; both are apparatus, not omitted narrative.

Abu Hurayra reports a Prophet prohibition mentioning dog price and mating compensation. Hindi lacks the explicit conjunction/male wording printed in Urdu; preserve the damaged concise wording without restoring those words.
The whole Urdu explicitly gives dog price and compensation for mating from a male. Preserve its own extra wording and remove only the terminal footnote marker.
Jabir finite report expressly attributes the cat-price prohibition to the Messenger. Whole source text is report, with no appended apparatus.
The complete own Urdu cat-price prohibition is supplied; keep it whole without adding broader animal-sale rules.

Ali reports Prophet cupping and his own payment. Hindi omits the Prophet ordered-me clause present in Urdu; no such instruction is inserted or asserted for this field. The cupper definition of hajjām is glossary context.
The Urdu actually supplies the Prophet command followed by Ali payment. Preserve that own predicate; only the parenthetic hajjām definition is context.
Abu Masud Uqba reports the Prophet prohibition of hajjām earnings. The parenthetic cupper definition is a lexical explanation; retain the actual term and prohibition.
The complete own Urdu supplied prohibition stays, with the cupper explanation separated as glossary context. Do not harmonize it with the adjacent payment account.
Abu Umama reports the three linked prohibitions concerning mughnia sale, earnings and consuming the price. The singing-women parenthesis defines the source term, not a separate narrated act.
Keep the entire supplied mughnia prohibition, while the singing-women definition is source glossary context. No grade or new qualification is added.

The source announces two sales but prints only the first, mulamasa, after the Prophet prohibition. Admit the actually supplied partial report with visible incompleteness; do not insert the second from Urdu. Trade is an English lexical gloss.
Urdu independently prints both mulamasa and munabadha. Both are actual report content; the terminal footnote marker alone is apparatus.

First Ibn Abbas transmits the Prophetic sale prohibition, then Tawus actually asks him about the phrase and receives his broker explanation. Both parts are supplied reports but the Companion interpretation is a distinct dialogue, not direct Prophet speech.
The full Urdu likewise has the first explicit prohibition and subsequent Tawus/Ibn Abbas question and answer. The short Arabic phrase is integral to that actual question, not an external locator.
Ibn Umar transmits the complete prohibition of going out to buy incoming trade goods before market arrival. Preserve that target and temporal boundary.
The own Urdu complete incoming-goods prohibition retains all source conditions; only its final footnote marker is context.
Ibn Masud expressly reports the Prophet prohibition of meeting sellers before they reach the market. The full field is supplied finite content.
The full Urdu source gives the same actual target and before-market condition; nothing is inferred from the neighboring similarly themed report.
Hakim ibn Hizam gives his own not-in-my-possession question and the Prophet do-not-sell reply. Keep this precise situation without expanding to a general ownership/legal formulation.
The complete own question and reply are supplied, with the source possession condition. Whole field is dialogue.

The Attab-to-Mecca report has damaged bridge/prohibition/spelling wording including ज़मीन. Preserve the literal finite report with its defect explicitly qualified; do not replace it with Urdu ضامن or add a missing clause.
Urdu independently supplies the Mecca sending and prohibition of profit without liability. Preserve its proper own wording without using it to repair Hindi.
Abu Hurayra reports the two named sale prohibitions. They are the actual supplied list; no definitions or extensions are added.
Both gharar and hasat are expressly supplied. The terminal footnote glyph is the only apparatus to separate.

Ibn Abbas report is a complete source-defective prohibition, with मन printed where the intended prohibition wording is damaged. Keep literal bytes and visible defect, without silently rewriting the vowel.
The complete Urdu prohibition is intact. Do not use it to silently repair the Hindi source.

Abu Said reports the complete list of unborn/udder/runaway/booty/charity/diver transactions with their birth, milk/measure, division and possession conditions. Diving-catch English is glossary context; no condition is omitted.

The actual parenthetic منع کیا clauses supply operative prohibitions for charity and diver cases and must remain. The loot synonym is a lexical gloss and the last footnote marker is apparatus. Preserve all timing/possession conditions.

Read the complete long Ansari episode: household goods, auction and two/three repetition, two-dirham distribution, axe fitting, collect-and-sell command, fifteen days, ten dirhams, purchases and three begging exceptions. The parenthetic and-sell command is an actual predicate and stays.

The entire long Urdu account independently supplies all stages, amounts, duration and three exceptions. Retain the parenthetic and-sell directive; it is not a gloss. Only the terminal footnote glyph is context.
Ali transmits the sunrise bargaining and milk-animal slaughter prohibitions. Suraj means the sun in this report, not a Surah label; retain the complete text.
The full Urdu preserves both prohibitions and sunrise timing; only the terminal footnote marker is apparatus. سورج is ordinary event wording, not a verse locator.
